legend: Busy Beaver is making a new language for his linguistics class! He has already decided that his language will have an alphabet whose letters are the integers 1,…,NM%%ZSMJ0%% in that order; now he wants to make some words for the language.

Because Busy Beaver is interested in statistics, he wants to control the frequencies of letters appearing in words, so he has chosen a multiset a%%ZSMJ1%% of size NM%%ZSMJ2%% of letters from his alphabet. He will now form N%%ZSMJ3%% words each with M%%ZSMJ4%% letters such that each letter from a%%ZSMJ5%% is used exactly once (i.e. if a given letter x%%ZSMJ6%% appears exactly k%%ZSMJ7%% times in a%%ZSMJ8%%, then it is used exactly k%%ZSMJ9%% times across all N%%ZSMJ10%% words).

After forming the words, Busy Beaver plans to organize them into a dictionary, so he will lexicographically sort his N%%ZSMJ11%% words to produce the sequence of words s1,…,sN%%ZSMJ12%%. Busy Beaver likes strings to be lexicographically small, so for each k%%ZSMJ13%% from 1%%ZSMJ14%% to N%%ZSMJ15%% he wants to know the lexicographically minimum possible value of sk%%ZSMJ16%% over all choices of words.

Note that the answer for each sk%%ZSMJ17%% is independent; for example, the choice of words so that s1%%ZSMJ18%% is minimized may be different from the choice of words so that s2%%ZSMJ19%% is minimized.
input: The first line contains two positive integers N,M%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤NM≤106%%ZSMJ21%%).
The second line contains NM%%ZSMJ22%% integers a1,…,aNM%%ZSMJ23%% composing the multiset a%%ZSMJ24%% (1≤aj≤NM%%ZSMJ25%%).
output: For each k%%ZSMJ26%% from 1%%ZSMJ27%% to N%%ZSMJ28%%, output the minimum possible value of sk%%ZSMJ29%% on its own line as a sequence of space-separated integers.
note: In the first sample, the following choices of words minimize each of sk%%ZSMJ30%%:
By choosing the words 112,233,445,566%%ZSMJ31%%, we get that s=112,233,445,566%%ZSMJ32%%, so s1=112%%ZSMJ33%% as desired.
By choosing the words 123,456,123,456%%ZSMJ34%%, we get that s=123,123,456,456%%ZSMJ35%%, so s2=123%%ZSMJ36%% as desired.
By choosing the words 166,155,344,223%%ZSMJ37%%, we get that s=155,166,223,344%%ZSMJ38%%, so s3=223%%ZSMJ39%% as desired.
By choosing the words 234,234,156,156%%ZSMJ40%%, we get that s=156,156,234,234%%ZSMJ41%%, so s4=234%%ZSMJ42%% as desired.
It can be shown that in all of these cases there is no way to choose the words so that the respective sk%%ZSMJ43%% is even lexicographically smaller.
